Each scheme uses the same 69-point protection algorithm to derive interval-specific allowances; spatial responses, input days and execution rules are unchanged. Panel (b) retains absolute quality values on a 0.2-percentage-point vertical span. The maximum within-policy range across binning schemes is 0.047 percentage points after rounding.

Figure M7. Nominal additional-point differences and paired conditional outer bounds: (a) complete ranges; (b) enlargement within −3 to 3 percentage points. In (b), dashed lines mark −0.2 percentage points for quality improvement and +0.2 for non-inferiority. Arrowheads indicate continuation of R10 beyond (b); its complete range is retained in (a). Red crosses and dashed ranges identify failed research acceptance for R18, R19, R20 and R22. Both configurations use the same 208 positions; contributions from identical executed states cancel. An invalid reference uses [0,1260] lx. Bounds require the declared 7% temporal, 5% full-task-plane shape and component-error conditions.
